# apple_subscription_introductory_offer_schedule (Resource)

Sets every introductory offer of an auto-renewable subscription.

This is the bulk counterpart to `apple_subscription_introductory_offer`. Apple keeps one introductory offer per territory, so a free trial in all 175 App Store storefronts through that resource means 175 resources and 175 API calls on apply. This resource creates new offers in a single `PATCH /v1/subscriptions/{id}` carrying them inline, and reads them all back in one listing. Removing an offer and changing an `end_date` still take one request each, because Apple publishes no bulk form for either.

An offer is matched to the one Apple holds by its territory, mode, duration, number of periods and price point (plus `start_date` and `target_subscription_plan_type` when they are set). A change to any of those removes the old offer and creates a new one; a change to `end_date` alone updates the offer in place.

Apple records a start date on every offer, the day it was created when none was given, and an import adopts it. After importing, set each `start_date` to Apple's value, or the first plan proposes removing them — an update that sends no requests, since an unset start date matches any.

~> **An `apple_subscription_availability` covering every territory has to exist first.** Nothing in an offer references one, so declare the ordering with `depends_on`.

Do not manage the same subscription with both this resource and `apple_subscription_introductory_offer`: every write here removes the offers it does not list, so an offer only the other resource knows about would be removed behind its back. `terraform destroy` deletes every offer this resource lists.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "apple_apps" "example" {
  bundle_id = "com.example.app"
}

resource "apple_subscription_group" "premium" {
  app_id         = data.apple_apps.example.apps[0].id
  reference_name = "Premium"
}

resource "apple_subscription" "pro_annual" {
  group_id            = apple_subscription_group.premium.id
  product_id          = "com.example.app.pro.annual"
  name                = "Pro Annual"
  subscription_period = "ONE_YEAR"
}

data "apple_territories" "all" {}

# Every territory an offer names has to be one the subscription sells in.
resource "apple_subscription_availability" "pro_annual" {
  subscription_id       = apple_subscription.pro_annual.id
  available_territories = data.apple_territories.all.ids
}

# The first three months at a reduced price in the United States, paid once.
data "apple_subscription_price_points" "usa_intro" {
  subscription_id = apple_subscription.pro_annual.id
  territories     = ["USA"]
  customer_price  = "19.99"
}

# A two-week free trial in every storefront except the United States, which
# gets the paid offer instead -- a territory holds one introductory offer at a
# time. Created in one API call, where the same fan-out through
# apple_subscription_introductory_offer is one resource and one POST per
# storefront.
resource "apple_subscription_introductory_offer_schedule" "pro_annual" {
  subscription_id = apple_subscription.pro_annual.id

  offers = concat(
    [
      for territory in data.apple_territories.all.ids : {
        territory_id      = territory
        offer_mode        = "FREE_TRIAL"
        duration          = "TWO_WEEKS"
        number_of_periods = 1
        # Spelled out so both halves of the concat have the same shape.
        price_point_id = null
      } if territory != "USA"
    ],
    [
      {
        territory_id      = "USA"
        offer_mode        = "PAY_UP_FRONT"
        duration          = "THREE_MONTHS"
        number_of_periods = 1
        price_point_id    = data.apple_subscription_price_points.usa_intro.price_points[0].id
      },
    ],
  )

  depends_on = [apple_subscription_availability.pro_annual]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `offers` (Attributes Set) The complete set of introductory offers the subscription should have, at most one per territory at a time. A set, because Apple returns them in no particular order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--offers))
- `subscription_id` (String) The ID of the `apple_subscription` these offers apply to. Cannot be changed after creation.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the subscription these offers belong to. A subscription has no separate record for its set of offers, so this mirrors `subscription_id`.

<a id="nestedatt--offers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `offers`

Required:

- `duration` (String) How long one offer period lasts: `THREE_DAYS`, `ONE_WEEK`, `TWO_WEEKS`, `ONE_MONTH`, `TWO_MONTHS`, `THREE_MONTHS`, `SIX_MONTHS` or `ONE_YEAR`. Apple restricts the combinations: for `PAY_AS_YOU_GO` it is the subscription's own period, and it validates the rest itself.
- `number_of_periods` (Number) How many `duration` periods the offer lasts. `1` for `FREE_TRIAL` and `PAY_UP_FRONT`; the number of discounted billing periods for `PAY_AS_YOU_GO`.
- `offer_mode` (String) What the customer pays during the offer: `FREE_TRIAL` (nothing), `PAY_AS_YOU_GO` (a reduced price every billing period for `number_of_periods` periods) or `PAY_UP_FRONT` (a reduced price once, for the whole `duration`).
- `territory_id` (String) The three-letter Apple territory code the offer applies in, for example `USA`, `GBR` or `EGY`. An introductory offer is always for one territory, and a territory holds one introductory offer at a time.

Optional:

- `end_date` (String) The last day the offer is available to new subscribers, as a plain date in `YYYY-MM-DD` form. Omit it for an offer with no end. This is the only attribute Apple allows to change on an existing offer.
- `price_point_id` (String) The price point the customer pays during a `PAY_AS_YOU_GO` or `PAY_UP_FRONT` offer. Required for those modes and rejected for `FREE_TRIAL`. Obtain it from the `apple_subscription_price_points` data source for this subscription and territory.
- `start_date` (String) The first day the offer is available to new subscribers, as a plain date in `YYYY-MM-DD` form. Omit it for an offer that starts immediately; Apple then records the day the offer was created as its start date.
- `target_subscription_plan_type` (String) Which plan the offer applies to: `MONTHLY` or `UPFRONT`. Omit it for an ordinary subscription.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# The import ID is the subscription ID. A subscription has no record of its own
# for its set of introductory offers, so they are reachable only through the
# collection hanging off it.
terraform import apple_subscription_introductory_offer_schedule.pro_annual 6740021496
```
